review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

20:1.sourceText: Τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ἔρχεται πρωῒ σκοτίας ἔτι οὔσης εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ βλέπει τὸν λίθον ἠρμένον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου.
20:1.targetText: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed from the entrance.

groups.note: The feminine μιᾷ ("one") implies ἡμέρᾳ and is rendered as the ordinal first; the dative of time supplies on.
The genitive absolute σκοτίας ἔτι οὔσης ("darkness still being") is rendered as a while-clause.
μνημείου ("tomb") is rendered entrance, the opening the stone had closed.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the noun day that the feminine μιᾷ implies; N1904 has no word for it.
English introduces a clause for the participle ἠρμένον ("taken away"); the Greek has no conjunction.

20:2.sourceText: τρέχει οὖν καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς Σίμωνα Πέτρον καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἄλλον μαθητὴν ὃν ἐφίλει ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἦραν τὸν Κύριον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου, καὶ οὐκ οἴδαμεν ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.
20:2.targetText: So she came running to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved. “They have taken the Lord out of the tomb,” she said, “and we do not know where they have put Him!”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB combines τρέχει καὶ ἔρχεται ("runs and comes") into came running, so καί has no separate word.
English does not repeat the preposition πρός ("to") before the other disciple.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB places she said inside the quotation, so this καί has no English counterpart.
BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a head for the relative clause.

20:3.sourceText: Ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Πέτρος καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητής, καὶ ἤρχοντο εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον.
20:3.targetText: Then Peter and the other disciple set out for the tomb.

groups.note: ἐξῆλθεν … καὶ ἤρχοντο ("went out … and were going") is rendered set out.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

20:4.sourceText: ἔτρεχον δὲ οἱ δύο ὁμοῦ· καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς προέδραμεν τάχιον τοῦ Πέτρου καὶ ἦλθεν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον,
20:4.targetText: The two were running together, but the other disciple outran Peter and reached the tomb first.

groups.note: This καί is contrastive; BSB renders it but.
προέδραμεν τάχιον ("ran ahead faster") is rendered outran.
ἦλθεν … εἰς ("came to") is rendered reached.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

20:5.sourceText: καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει κείμενα τὰ ὀθόνια, οὐ μέντοι εἰσῆλθεν.
20:5.targetText: He bent down and looked in at the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.

groups.note: βλέπει ("sees") is rendered looked in at.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle παρακύψας, rendered bent down, to the main verb.

20:6.sourceText: ἔρχεται οὖν καὶ Σίμων Πέτρος ἀκολουθῶν αὐτῷ, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ θεωρεῖ τὰ ὀθόνια κείμενα,
20:6.targetText: Simon Peter arrived just after him. He entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there.

groups.note: The participle ἀκολουθῶν ("following") is rendered just after.
εἰσῆλθεν εἰς ("went into") is rendered entered.

20:7.sourceText: καὶ τὸ σουδάριον, ὃ ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ, οὐ μετὰ τῶν ὀθονίων κείμενον ἀλλὰ χωρὶς ἐντετυλιγμένον εἰς ἕνα τόπον.
20:7.targetText: The cloth that had been around Jesus’ head was rolled up, lying separate from the linen cloths.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered Jesus’.
οὐ μετὰ … ἀλλὰ χωρίς ("not with … but apart") is rendered separate from.

20:8.sourceText: τότε οὖν εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς ὁ ἐλθὼν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ εἶδεν καὶ ἐπίστευσεν·
20:8.targetText: Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in. And he saw and believed.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἐλθών … εἰς ("the one who came to") is rendered who had reached.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.

20:9.sourceText: οὐδέπω γὰρ ᾔδεισαν τὴν γραφὴν, ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι.
20:9.targetText: For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.

groups.note: οὐδέπω ("not yet") is rendered still … not.
ᾔδεισαν ("they knew") is rendered understand.
The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered Jesus.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the preposition; τὴν γραφήν is the direct object of ᾔδεισαν.

20:10.sourceText: ἀπῆλθον οὖν πάλιν πρὸς αὑτοὺς οἱ μαθηταί.
20:10.targetText: Then the disciples returned to their homes.

groups.note: ἀπῆλθον … πάλιν ("went away again") is rendered returned.
The reflexive αὑτούς ("themselves") is rendered their homes.

20:11.sourceText: Μαρία δὲ εἱστήκει πρὸς τῷ μνημείῳ ἔξω κλαίουσα. ὡς οὖν ἔκλαιεν, παρέκυψεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον,
20:11.targetText: But Mary stood outside the tomb weeping. And as she wept, she bent down to look into the tomb,

groups.note: πρὸς … ἔξω ("at … outside") is rendered outside.
παρέκυψεν ("stooped to look") is rendered bent down to look.

20:12.sourceText: καὶ θεωρεῖ δύο ἀγγέλους ἐν λευκοῖς καθεζομένους, ἕνα πρὸς τῇ κεφαλῇ καὶ ἕνα πρὸς τοῖς ποσίν, ὅπου ἔκειτο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
20:12.targetText: and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet.

groups.note: The second ἕνα ("one") is rendered the other.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

20:13.sourceText: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῇ ἐκεῖνοι Γύναι, τί κλαίεις; λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ἦραν τὸν Κύριόν μου, καὶ οὐκ οἶδα ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.
20:13.targetText: “Woman, why are you weeping?” they asked.  “Because they have taken my Lord away,” she said, “and I do not know where they have put Him.”

groups.note: ὅτι introduces her answer and is rendered Because.
ἦραν ("they took away") is rendered have taken … away.

20:14.sourceText: ταῦτα εἰποῦσα ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω, καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἑστῶτα, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν.
20:14.targetText: When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there; but she did not recognize that it was Jesus.

groups.note: The participle εἰποῦσα ("having said") is rendered as a When-clause.
εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω ("to the things behind") is rendered around.
This καί is contrastive; BSB renders it but.
ᾔδει ("she knew") is rendered recognize.

20:15.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς Γύναι, τί κλαίεις; τίνα ζητεῖς; ἐκείνη δοκοῦσα ὅτι ὁ κηπουρός ἐστιν, λέγει αὐτῷ Κύριε, εἰ σὺ ἐβάστασας αὐτόν, εἰπέ μοι ποῦ ἔθηκας αὐτόν, κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἀρῶ.
20:15.targetText: “Woman, why are you weeping?” Jesus asked. “Whom are you seeking?”  Thinking He was the gardener, she said, “Sir, if you have carried Him off, tell me where you have put Him, and I will get Him.”

groups.note: ἐβάστασας ("you carried away") is rendered have carried … off.
κἀγώ is καί + ἐγώ, "and I".

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῇ ("to her") is not rendered.

20:16.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς Μαριάμ. στραφεῖσα ἐκείνη λέγει αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστί· Ῥαββουνεί (ὃ λέγεται Διδάσκαλε).

20:17.targetText: “Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”

groups.note: The one πρός ("to") governs both pairs; English repeats to before My God.

20:19.sourceText: Οὔσης οὖν ὀψίας τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ τῇ μιᾷ σαββάτων, καὶ τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων ὅπου ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.
20:19.targetText: It was the first day of the week, and that very evening, while the disciples were together with the doors locked for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them. “Peace be with you!” He said to them.

groups.note: The participle Οὔσης ("being"), with evening, is rendered It was.
ἐκείνῃ ("that"), said of the day, is rendered that very with evening.
The feminine μιᾷ ("one") agrees with ἡμέρᾳ and is rendered as the ordinal first.
The genitive absolute τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων ("the doors having been shut") is rendered with the doors locked.
ὅπου ἦσαν ("where … were") is rendered were together.
εἰς τὸ μέσον ("into the middle") is rendered among them.
